$comment: Production record, 29 Aug 2026, UNMODIFIED. DIALECT B, and ACCEPTED since T-063 (8 Sep 2026): Q15a was answered on 4 Sep (DL-105) with 'make it work for all the known dialects', which reverses ADR-007 §4 and supersedes DL-089. It moved here from invalid/ when the schema gained the closed three-dialect enumeration, and the $expect: writer-dlq marker it used to carry went with it. Bare field names, but every counter is a STRING ("176"), plus rx_type_arol and no timespan at all. The Writer coerces these per field, range-checked against the signed BIGINT maximum BEFORE conversion; a value that does not parse or that overflows DEAD-LETTERS - never zeroed, never truncated, never defaulted, which is the int4-wrapping shape of trap 11 (DL-105 rule 3). invalid/lorastats-dialect-string-overflow.json is the fixture that holds that line. It carries version:1, the same as the other two dialects, so nothing on the record could have discriminated it (trap 20). NOTE: production sends tenant == maintenant == "mzc", which is exactly the trap in claude/CLAUDE.md §6. This fixture is kept byte-faithful because its job is to be a production regression guard; it is NOT an isolation test. The *-tenant-isolation-pair.json fixtures, where the two values deliberately differ, remain the only isolation guards.
